findings.description: validate_regateverdict_criteria_outcomes treats criteria_outcomes as a dict (using 'c not in outcomes'), but gate-verdict.schema.json defines criteria_outcomes as an array of objects with criterion/status/evidence fields. A schema-valid verdict would have criteria_outcomes as a list of dicts, so 'c not in outcomes' would always evaluate to True (string never found in a list of dicts), causing every criterion to appear missing and triggering false escalations in the re-gate path.
findings.evidence: remediation_controller.py line 302: outcomes = verdict.get('criteria_outcomes', {}); line 303: missing = [c for c in frozen_criteria if c not in outcomes]. Schema at core/state/gate-verdict.schema.json lines 80-94 defines criteria_outcomes as 'type: array' with items containing criterion/status/evidence. Tests in TestValidateRegateVerdictCriteriaOutcomes all use dict-format criteria_outcomes (not schema-compliant), so tests pass but function would fail on real agent verdicts.
